Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

condition noun

something that must be met first

also on condition that, provided that, providing, on one condition

classical

Cic. Arch. 25: sed eā condiciōne, nē quid posteā scrīberet
Phaedr. 3.13.12: apibus condiciō placet
Traupman 295

condiciō, condiciōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

condition, terms

“On condition that” is eā condiciōne ut (or nē) with the subjunctive; to turn down the terms, condiciōnem respuere (Caes. BG 1.42, Lewis & Short). The spelling conditiō is a manuscript error that took the word for a derivative of condō (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • lēx, lēgis f. — condition, terms (of an agreement)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 102: hāc lēge tibi meam adstringō fidem; Traupman 95: eā lēge ut; Traupman 295 · Declension on Wiktionary

    (sēnsus plērumque cōmicus: Plaut., Ter.; also Cato)

    Hāc lēge, eā lēge ut, on these terms; in this sense mostly before Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • dum, dummodo — provided that, so long as

    conjunctions, with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Accius in Cic. Off. 1.97: ōderint, dum metuant; Cic. Brut. 285: dummodo sit polīta (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    The negative is dum nē, dummodo nē.

  • sī modo — if only, provided that

    conjunction with an adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.48: sī modo possīs

Examples

  • jubēre eī praemium tribuī, sed eā condiciōne, nē quid posteā scrīberet

    (we saw Sulla) order a reward to be given him, but on condition that he write nothing moreCic. Arch. 25

  • vērum heus tū, hāc lēge tibi meam adstringō fidem: quae vēra audīvī taceō et contineō optumē

    but listen, I give you my word on this condition: what I hear that’s true, I keep to myself and hold in perfectlyTer. Eun. 102–103

  • fūcī recūsant: apibus condiciō placet

    the drones refuse; the bees accept the termsPhaedr. 3.13.12

See also state, situation.
